title: OHS Incident Reporting and LACES Process
cross_references: SOP J08.01 - OH&S Incident Response - Class 1 Emergencies

nodes.text: Use OHS Incident Report Card (salmon coloured) to record incidents, injuries, near misses, and hazards

evidence.source_text: The OHS Incident Report Card (salmon coloured) is used to record incidents, injuries, near misses and hazards at bushfires.

nodes.text: Provide completed card to Logistics Officer or medical services unit leader

evidence.source_text: The completed card is to be provided to the Logistics Officer, (or medical services unit leader if in place).

nodes.text: Immediately communicate incidents via chain of command

evidence.source_text: This does not replace the need to immediately communicate these incidents via the chain of command.

nodes.text: Report OHS incidents via own agency’s reporting system

evidence.source_text: Personnel will be required to report OHS incidents via their own agency’s reporting system.

nodes.text: Deploy lookouts to maintain risk awareness and provide timely advice

evidence.source_text: A fixed, aerial or mobile lookout shall be deployed to maintain a clear appreciation of risks and to provide timely advice of the need to use of escape routes and safety zones.

nodes.text: Ensure firefighters are aware of changes in fire behaviour and hazards

evidence.source_text: Firefighters shall be aware of the impact of changes in fire behaviour including those resulting from variations to fuel, weather and topography and of other fireground hazards.

nodes.text: Follow Communications Plan and address safety issues

evidence.source_text: All fire crews shall follow the Communications Plan, communicate with your crew and surrounding crews to discuss and address safety issues.

nodes.text: Agree on and review at least two escape routes

evidence.source_text: At least two escape routes should be agreed and made known to all relevant personnel. The suitability of an escape route should be continually reviewed to ensure it remains effective.
Safety zones should be identified and made known to all relevant firefighters. Firefighters need to consider escape time and safety zone size requirements that will change as fire behaviour changes.

nodes.text: OHS Incident Reporting and LACES process complete

evidence.source_text: SOP J08.01 - OH&S Incident Response - Class 1 Emergencies provide further information.
